summary: Stale routing entry sent traffic to quantized variant incompatible with GPU kernels, causing upstream runtime OOMs and API gateway 5xx wave
description: Issue summary: Customer NimbleDocs observed a sudden spike in 502/503 responses for generation and embedding requests from ~18:05->18:55 UTC. Impact: customer-facing errors and degraded throughput for several reserved pools. Environment: prod us-east-1 on Dedicated pool servicing NimbleDocs with model pinned to a named variant. Immediate symptom: API gateway returning 502/503; serving runtime processes showing repeated worker exits with 'cuMemAlloc' and 'kernel not found' style errors.
impact: NimbleDocs saw ~35% failed requests for 50m window, several user-facing errors in their product. Elevated latency and retries increased token costs. No data loss reported; requests retried by gateway produced additional load and amplified the problem.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send concurrent long-context generation requests (~30k token prompt mix) to NimbleDocs tenant route in prod-us-east-1
2) Observe apigw returning 502/503 and backoff retries from client
3) Check serving-runtime logs to see worker exit traces and NVML/gpu allocation failures
4) Correlate with routing table snapshot to see route pointing at pool with quantized variant marked 'legacy-quant'
logs: 2026-03-13T18:07:12Z runtime[worker-23]: ERROR cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory (500)
2026-03-13T18:07:13Z runtime[worker-23]: WARN requested kernel 'qkernel_v2' not found for model nimble-docs/redwood-3b-quant-v2
2026-03-13T18:07:13Z apigw[proxy-11]: upstream returned 502 when talking to 10.2.45.23:8080
2026-03-13T18:12:04Z autoscaler: detected repeated worker exits, marking pool unhealthy and initiating warm replacements
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: GPU OOM due to unexpectedly long prompts + quantized memory layout mismatch increasing allocation pressure.
Observed that routing controlplane pushed a route delta at 2026-03-13T17:58:01Z that included a stale backend pool id (pool-legacy-quant) which was previously decommissioned but not fully drained.

Pool pool-legacy-quant still contained a model variant built with an older quant kernel set (qkernel_v2) that our current runtime no longer bundles by default on new GPUs, causing fallback attempts and failed allocations.

Amplification path: apigw retries + hedged retry behavior sent duplicate load to the unhealthy pool while healthchecks were still passing intermittently, causing repeated OOMs and eventual worker exits.

root_cause: A stale routing entry directed production traffic to a legacy backend pool hosting a model variant compiled against an older quantization kernel set that was incompatible with the runtime image on current GPU hosts. The incompatibility led to fallback allocation attempts, increased memory pressure, and repeated cuMemAlloc failures culminating in worker exits and 5xx responses from the API gateway.
resolution: Diverted traffic off pool-legacy-quant, drained and cordoned the legacy pool, and applied an emergency controlplane fix to ensure route cache invalidation occurs after route deltas. Restarted affected serving-runtime processes and verified model variant compatibility before reintroducing to traffic.
resolution_notes: 1) Route divert executed at 2026-03-13T18:28:44Z by infra on-call (Daniel C.).
2) Legacy pool cordoned and removed from routing at 2026-03-13T18:35:01Z.
3) Rolling restart of 8 runtime nodes completed by 19:10 UTC; health checks passed.
4) Customer NimbleDocs confirmed successful request flow and reduced error rates by 19:15 UTC.
follow_up_tasks: TASK-1: Add a preflight compatibility check in the controlplane to reject route entries that point to pools with model variants not present in the runtime's kernel manifest. Owner: infra-team. ETA: 2026-03-20
TASK-2: Implement explicit route cache flush confirmation after route delta application. Owner: controlplane. ETA: 2026-03-17
TASK-3: Add alerting for mismatched model kernel versions between pool manifest and runtime image. Owner: monitoring. ETA: 2026-03-18
TASK-4: Post-incident blameless review and update runbook (confluence). Owner: on-call rotation. ETA: 2026-03-19
